questions.question: What role does the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) play in India’s space missions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Development of launch vehicles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC)**, headquartered in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, is the main center of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** focused on the development of **launch vehicles**.
 
• VSSC is responsible for designing and developing **various types of rockets and launch systems** that are crucial for India's space programs, including **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle), GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle), and GSLV Mk-III**.
 
• VSSC contributes to the **development of propulsion systems, aerodynamics, flight dynamics, avionics, and vehicle integration**, which are essential for the success of launch missions.
 
• The center has played a pivotal role in India's achievements in space exploration, such as the **Chandrayaan missions** and **Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)**, by providing reliable launch vehicles.
 
• It operates under the **Department of Space, Government of India**, and is named after **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**, regarded as the father of the Indian space program.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC):**

 
 
• Located in **Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala**, VSSC is one of the largest ISRO centers specializing in **rocket and launch vehicle development**.
 
• It is involved in the creation of advanced technologies such as **cryogenic engines**, reusable launch vehicles, and space transportation systems.
 
• The center has collaborated with other ISRO centers like the **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)** and the **SATISH Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)** for successful launch operations.
 
• VSSC played a major role in the **Chandrayaan-3 mission**, ensuring the successful propulsion of the lunar lander.
 
 
 
• **Other ISRO Centers:**
 
 
• **SATISH Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC):** Located in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, this center is responsible for **launch vehicle integration and launch operations.**
 
• **U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC):** Located in Bengaluru, Karnataka, it focuses on the development of **satellites** for communication, remote sensing, and navigation.
 
• **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC):** Handles the development of **liquid propulsion systems** used in launch vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Indian Space Missions:**
 
 
• **PSLV:** Known as the workhorse of ISRO, PSLV is used for launching satellites into polar orbits.
 
• **GSLV:** Used for launching heavier satellites into geosynchronous orbits, powered by **cryogenic engines**.
 
• **GSLV Mk-III:** The most powerful launch vehicle developed by ISRO, capable of carrying heavy payloads, including the **Chandrayaan-2 mission.**
 
 
 
• **Important Contributions:**
 
 
• Development of **Reusable Launch Vehicles (RLV)** and **Small Satellite Launch Vehicles (SSLV)** for cost-effective space exploration.
 
• Support in international collaborations such as **Artemis missions** with NASA.
 
• India's entry into the **commercial satellite launch market** through the **Antrix Corporation**, ISRO's commercial wing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satellite Tracking Operations:**

 
 
• Satellite tracking is primarily handled by centers like the **Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN)** in Bengaluru.
 
• It ensures communication with satellites and interplanetary missions.
 
 
 
• **Training of Space Scientists:**
 
 
• Space scientist training is carried out at **ISRO's Space Applications Centre (SAC)** and **Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST).**
 
 
 
• **Mission Control Management:**
 
 
• Mission control is conducted at **ISRO's Mission Operations Complex (MOX)**, Bengaluru, which handles spacecraft operations and telemetry.

questions.question: The Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) aims to strengthen innovation and entrepreneurship. Which initiative functions under AIM?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atal Tinkering Labs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)** is a flagship initiative by the **Government of India** under the **NITI Aayog**, aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship across the country.
 
• The **Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs)** are a significant initiative under AIM, established to cultivate curiosity, creativity, and imagination in young minds through hands-on learning and innovation in schools.
 
• **ATLs** are equipped with tools and equipment such as robotics kits, 3D printers, and sensors to enable students to work on projects and problem-solving using new-age technology.
 
• The primary objective of these labs is to create a robust innovation ecosystem in schools by encouraging scientific temper, computational thinking, and digital literacy among students.
 
• Since its inception, AIM has set up **10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs** across India, benefiting students from classes 6 to 12, particularly in remote and underprivileged regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Features of Atal Tinkering Labs:**

 
 
• ATLs are designed for students in the age group of **12–18 years** to foster a problem-solving mindset and advance their skills in technology and innovation.
 
• Each lab is provided with financial support of up to **20 lakh INR** over a five-year period, which includes the cost of setting up the lab and operational expenses.
 
• Students get access to cutting-edge tools and resources such as **robotics kits, 3D printers, microcontrollers**, and sensors to build prototypes and innovative projects.
 
• ATLs also conduct workshops, hackathons, and competitions to promote peer learning and engagement with industry experts.
 
 
 
• **Other Initiatives under AIM:**
 
 
• **Atal Incubation Centres (AICs):** These centers provide support to startups by offering infrastructure, mentoring, and funding opportunities to accelerate entrepreneurship.
 
• **Atal New India Challenges (ANICs):** These are aimed at fostering product innovations and aligning them with national development priorities.
 
• **Mentor India Initiative:** Aimed at engaging leaders and experts from various industries to mentor students and startups under AIM's initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Atal Tinkering Labs:**
 
 
• Encourages a **culture of innovation** and entrepreneurship among school students.
 
• Bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application through experiential learning.
 
• Focuses on building skills in **STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics)**, which are essential for the workforce of the future.
 
• Promotes inclusivity by providing opportunities to students from all socio-economic backgrounds.
 
 
 
• **Options Analysis:**
 
 
• **Option 1: National Skill Centres** - These are not directly linked to AIM but are part of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship's initiatives.
 
• **Option 2: Startup Seed Assistance** - While this is related to entrepreneurship, it is not a specific program under AIM.
 
• **Option 3: Atal Tinkering Labs** - Correct; this is a flagship initiative under AIM.
 
• **Option 4: PM Kaushal Programme** - This is a skill development initiative and not part of AIM.

questions.question: The merger of princely states with India after 1947 was influenced by multiple forces. Which factor most weakened the rulers’ desire to remain independent?

options.text: Strong military pressure from neighbouring countries
Public movements supporting integration with India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public movements supporting integration with India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After **India’s independence in 1947**, the integration of princely states into India became a crucial task. Public movements strongly influenced this process by advocating for national unity and integration.
 
• Several princely states witnessed mass movements where citizens demanded **merger with India**, rejecting the idea of remaining independent or joining Pakistan. This created significant pressure on rulers to accede to India.
 
• Leaders like **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** and **V.P. Menon** utilized public sentiment to negotiate with rulers effectively, showcasing the people's desire for integration.
 
• The role of the **Indian National Congress** and other political organizations in organizing campaigns and fostering nationalistic fervor further weakened the rulers' resolve to remain independent.
 
• In many princely states, the public showed overwhelming support for merging with India due to shared cultural, linguistic, and historical ties, which undermined the rulers' efforts to maintain autonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Integration of Princely States:**

 
 
• At the time of independence, there were **565 princely states** in India, and they were given the choice to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, India’s first Home Minister, played a pivotal role in persuading the rulers to merge with India.
 
• Techniques such as **negotiation, diplomacy, and military intervention** were used to achieve integration.
 
• Important examples include the accession of **Hyderabad** (via Operation Polo), **Kashmir** (via Instrument of Accession), and **Junagadh** (via plebiscite).
 
 
 
• **Role of Public Movements:**
 
 
• In states like **Junagadh**, **Kashmir**, and **Hyderabad**, public movements were instrumental in influencing political decisions.
 
• The **Indian National Congress** and other organizations mobilized citizens to demand integration, emphasizing the importance of a unified India.
 
• Mass protests, rallies, and petitions showcased the overwhelming public sentiment against independence or joining Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Other Factors Influencing Integration:**
 
 
• **Military Pressure:** In cases like Hyderabad, military action (Operation Polo) was taken to integrate the state when negotiations failed.
 
• **Economic Constraints:** Many princely states lacked economic self-sufficiency and recognized the need to merge with India for stability and development.
 
• **Lack of British Support:** With the end of British rule, princely states lost their patronage, making independence unsustainable.
 
 
 
• **Key Examples:**
 
 
• **Junagadh:** Public protests led to a plebiscite, where the majority voted for accession to India.
 
• **Kashmir:** The decision to accede was influenced by public sentiment and military intervention during the tribal invasion.
 
• **Hyderabad:** The integration was achieved through military action following public unrest and political instability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Instrument of Accession:**

 
 
• This legal document allowed princely states to join India or Pakistan. It outlined the terms of accession and guaranteed certain rights to rulers.
 
• Most states signed the Instrument of Accession, agreeing to transfer control of defense, foreign affairs, and communications to India.
 
 
 
• **Operation Polo:**
 
 
• This military operation was conducted in **September 1948** to integrate Hyderabad into India following the refusal of its ruler to accede.
 
• It resulted in the annexation of Hyderabad and demonstrated India’s resolve to maintain unity.

questions.question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) was introduced primarily as part of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Overhauling colonial-era criminal laws**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (**BNS**) aims to **replace colonial-era criminal laws**, specifically the Indian Penal Code (IPC), Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), and the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
 
• Introduced in **2023**, the BNS seeks to modernize and adapt laws to India's contemporary socio-political and cultural realities.
 
• The colonial-era IPC, drafted in **1860**, has been criticized for being outdated and unreflective of modern principles of justice and fairness.
 
• The overhaul under BNS aims to simplify legal procedures, ensure faster delivery of justice, and **decriminalize minor offenses** to reduce the burden on courts.
 
• The BNS emphasizes a victim-centric approach, enhancing provisions for victim compensation and rights within the legal framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Colonial-era criminal laws:**

 
 
• The **Indian Penal Code (IPC)**, enacted in **1860**, served as the backbone of criminal law in India, but its provisions reflect colonial priorities rather than modern Indian realities.
 
• The **Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC)**, implemented in **1973**, governs procedural aspects of criminal law but requires modernization to adapt to modern advancements.
 
• The **Indian Evidence Act**, passed in **1872**, outlines rules regarding evidence in trials, but some provisions are considered restrictive and outdated.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita:**
 
 
• **Modernization:** The BNS seeks to align criminal laws with the **Constitution of India** and contemporary legal practices.
 
• **Victim-Centric Approach:** It emphasizes **victim compensation** and ensures their rights are adequately protected during legal proceedings.
 
• **Decriminalization:** Minor offenses are being decriminalized to reduce the burden on the judicial system.
 
• **Transparency:** The laws promote transparent legal processes to ensure fairness and justice.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Reforming Family Laws:** This relates to personal laws such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption, but is unrelated to the BNS.
 
• **Implementing Tax Reforms:** Tax reforms focus on financial policies like GST, corporate tax, etc., and are not connected to criminal law.
 
• **Expanding International Trade Laws:** This pertains to global commerce and trade agreements, which are entirely distinct from the scope of the BNS.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita was introduced to **replace outdated colonial laws** that no longer align with the modern principles of justice.
 
• It aims to ensure **speedy justice** by simplifying legal procedures and focusing on victim rights.
 
• The BNS aligns criminal laws with the **Indian Constitution** and modern values, ensuring that they reflect **India's current socio-political realities**.

questions.question: Digboi, Moran, Sivasagar, and Naharkatiya oil fields are situated in which region of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North-Eastern region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Digboi, Moran, Sivasagar, and Naharkatiya oil fields** are located in the **North-Eastern region** of India, specifically in the state of **Assam**.
 
• Digboi is renowned for being India's **oldest oil refinery**, established in **1901**, and is often referred to as the **"Oil City of Assam"**.
 
• Moran and Naharkatiya are other significant oil fields in Assam, contributing substantially to India's **domestic crude oil production**.
 
• The North-Eastern region is known for its **rich hydrocarbon reserves**, especially crude oil and natural gas, which are vital for India's energy sector.
 
• Sivasagar, historically an important town in Assam, is also a key location for **oil exploration and production**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significance of Assam in India's Oil Industry:**

 
 
• Assam was the first state in India to discover oil, with the first successful oil well drilled in **Digboi in 1889**.
 
• The Digboi refinery, established in **1901**, is the **oldest operational refinery in the world**.
 
• Assam's oil fields contribute a significant percentage of India's **domestic crude oil production**, making the state a vital energy hub.
 
 
 
• **North-Eastern Region's Role in Hydrocarbon Exploration:**
 
 
• The region is rich in **hydrocarbon reserves**, including both crude oil and natural gas.
 
• Key companies like **Oil India Limited (OIL)** and **ONGC** are actively involved in exploration and production in this region.
 
• The government has initiated several policies to enhance exploration and production in the North-Eastern region under the **Hydrocarbon Vision 2030**.
 
 
 
• **Features of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Western Ghats:** Known for its biodiversity, the Western Ghats are not associated with significant oil fields. Instead, they are renowned for **ecotourism and agriculture**.
 
• **Central Highlands:** While rich in minerals like iron ore and manganese, this region does not have significant hydrocarbon reserves.
 
• **Eastern Coastal Plains:** This region is known for its fertile lands and ports, with some offshore oil and gas fields but not the ones mentioned in the question.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The North-Eastern region's oil production is crucial for India's energy security, reducing reliance on **oil imports**.
 
• Efforts are being made to improve infrastructure in the region to facilitate **transportation and refining** of crude oil.
 
• The government has prioritized the development of this region under various schemes such as the **North East Industrial Development Scheme (NEIDS)**.

questions.question:
Consider the following landforms:

1. Tors

2. Spurs

3. Block Mountains

Which of these are found in the Peninsular Plateau of India?

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is '1, 2 and 3'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tors:**

 
 
• Tors are isolated rock outcrops formed due to **weathering and erosion**, commonly seen in granitic regions.
 
• They are a characteristic feature of the **Peninsular Plateau**, especially in areas with ancient crystalline rocks.
 
• **Example:** Hampi (Karnataka) is famous for its granite tors and boulder landscapes.
 
 
 
• **Spurs:**
 
 
• Spurs are **projecting ridges** that extend from hills or mountains, formed due to river erosion.
 
• They are present in the dissected plateau regions where rivers have carved valleys.
 
• **Example:** The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats show several spurs formed by river systems.
 
 
 
• **Block Mountains:**
 
 
• Block mountains are formed due to **faulting**, where large crustal blocks are uplifted or downthrown.
 
• The Peninsular Plateau has several such features due to its **tectonic stability and ancient faults**.
 
• **Example:** The Vindhya and Satpura ranges are classic examples of block mountains in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is composed of **ancient igneous and metamorphic rocks**, making it geologically stable.
 
• It has undergone prolonged **denudation**, leading to the formation of diverse landforms like tors and residual hills.
 
• Faulting and tectonic movements in the past have contributed to the formation of **block mountains and rift valleys** such as the Narmada valley.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Peninsular Plateau is one of the **oldest landmasses** of the Earth.
 
• It exhibits a variety of **erosional and structural landforms**.
 
• Hence, all the given landforms—tors, spurs, and block mountains—are found in this region.

questions.question: Which materials were mainly used in the construction of Purana Qila?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sandstone and marble**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Purana Qila**, also known as the Old Fort, is one of the oldest forts in Delhi, India, and is a significant example of Mughal architecture.
 
• The primary materials used in the construction of the fort were **sandstone** and **marble**, which were commonly utilized during the Mughal era for their durability and aesthetic appeal.
 
• **Sandstone**, particularly red and buff sandstone, was extensively used for the walls, gateways, and other structural components of Purana Qila, providing the fort with its iconic and majestic look.
 
• **Marble** was employed for decorative elements and intricate inlays, adding a touch of elegance and sophistication to the fort's architecture.
 
• The fort was constructed during the reigns of **Sher Shah Suri** (1540-1545) and later completed by **Humayun**, reflecting a blend of Islamic and Afghan architectural styles.

questions.question: The drainage system of Mohenjodaro was remarkable because houses were linked to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Covered street drains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The drainage system of **Mohenjodaro**, part of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, was highly advanced and considered remarkable for its time.
 
• Each house in Mohenjodaro was connected to a network of **covered street drains**, which ensured proper disposal of waste water and maintained hygiene in urban spaces.
 
• The street drains were constructed using bricks and were covered with stone slabs, which could be removed for cleaning—a feature showing advanced urban planning and sanitation techniques.
 
• The drains were laid out systematically along the streets and were designed to carry sewage and rainwater away from residential and public areas. 
 
• This innovative drainage system demonstrates the emphasis placed by the Indus Valley Civilization on cleanliness, urban planning, and public health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization:**

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, flourished around **2600–1900 BCE** in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• It is renowned for its advanced urban planning, including features like **grid-patterned streets, sewage systems, and standardized brick sizes**.
 
• Prominent sites of the civilization include Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
 
 
• **Features of Mohenjodaro’s Drainage System:**
 
 
• Drains were **lined with bricks** and covered with slabs, ensuring durability and ease of maintenance.
 
• Manholes were provided at regular intervals to facilitate cleaning, showing the meticulous planning of the system.
 
• The drainage system was connected to soak pits and larger drains, ensuring efficient waste disposal.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Ancient Civilizations:**
 
 
• The drainage system of the Indus Valley Civilization was far more advanced compared to contemporary civilizations like Mesopotamia and Egypt.
 
• While Mesopotamia had open drains, the covered and interconnected system in Mohenjodaro shows greater sophistication.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Urban Planning:**
 
 
• The planning reflects the civic management and the high priority given to sanitation by the people of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• It demonstrates the use of technology and systematic thinking to enhance public health and urban living standards.

questions.question: Apart from rocky terrain, what was a major agricultural challenge in the Chola period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Limited irrigation facilities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• During the **Chola period**, agriculture faced significant challenges due to **limited irrigation facilities**.
 
• The Chola rulers made considerable efforts to improve irrigation systems, including the construction of tanks, canals, and water reservoirs to support agriculture.
 
• The rocky terrain in many parts of the Chola empire made it difficult to expand irrigation systems, increasing dependence on monsoon rains for cultivation.
 
• Agriculture during this period primarily depended on the availability of water from rivers like the **Kaveri**, and the establishment of irrigation infrastructure was critical for ensuring productivity.
 
• Despite the challenges, the Cholas were known for their administrative efficiency in maintaining and developing water management systems to overcome these limitations.

questions.question: The Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project connects India with which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project** is a significant connectivity initiative undertaken by **India and Myanmar**.
 
• It aims to connect the **eastern Indian seaport of Kolkata** with the **Sittwe Port in Myanmar** through a multimodal transport system consisting of sea, river, and roadways.
 
• The project involves **shipping from Kolkata to Sittwe**, followed by inland water transport along the Kaladan River to Paletwa in Myanmar, and a road link from Paletwa to the Indian border in Mizoram.
 
• The initiative is expected to boost **trade and economic cooperation** between India and Myanmar while also improving connectivity to the northeastern states of India.
 
• The project was first proposed in **2008** and is being implemented under the **Act East Policy** of India to enhance connectivity with Southeast Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of the Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project:**

 
 
• The project is a **multi-modal transport initiative** that combines **sea, river, and road connectivity**.
 
• The sea route connects the **Kolkata Port in India** to the **Sittwe Port in Myanmar**, a distance of approximately 539 km.
 
• The inland waterway component involves a **158 km route along the Kaladan River**, connecting Sittwe Port to Paletwa in Myanmar.
 
• The final phase is the construction of a **110 km road link** from Paletwa to the **Mizoram border** in India.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Project:**
 
 
• It provides an **alternative route** to India's northeastern states, bypassing the **narrow Siliguri Corridor (Chicken’s Neck)**.
 
• The project enhances **India-Myanmar relations** and strengthens India's presence in Southeast Asia under the **Act East Policy**.
 
• It is designed to improve **trade and economic integration** between India and the ASEAN region.
 
• The initiative also aims to spur **infrastructure development** and economic growth in the remote northeastern regions of India.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• The Kaladan project is a critical part of India's efforts to **counter Chinese influence** in Myanmar and Southeast Asia.
 
• It opens up new transit and transport routes, enhancing **India's regional connectivity**.
 
• The project also contributes to **security and stability** in the northeastern states by improving economic opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Implementation:**
 
 
• The project has faced delays due to **security concerns** in Myanmar, particularly in the Rakhine state.
 
• Issues such as **funding, logistics, and coordination** between India and Myanmar have also slowed progress.
 
• Despite these challenges, the project remains a priority for India’s foreign policy objectives in the region.

questions.question: As of mid-2025, which statement accurately reflects Ajit Doval’s position as National Security Advisor?

options.text: First independent tenure after advisory role
Holds rank equal to Cabinet Secretary
Reappointed in 2024; tenure co-terminus with PM

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reappointed in 2024; tenure co-terminus with PM​.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ajit Doval** has served as India’s **National Security Advisor (NSA)** since **2014** under **Narendra Modi**.
 
• In **June 2024**, the Government of India **reappointed him for a third consecutive term** as NSA.
 
• The official order states that **his tenure is “co-terminus with the term of the Prime Minister or until further orders.” **

**​​Why other options are incorrect?**__

__
 
• **First independent tenure after advisory role** – Incorrect. Doval has been NSA continuously since **2014**, not in a first independent tenure.
 
• **Holds rank equal to Cabinet Secretary** – Incorrect. He is given the **rank of a Cabinet Minister in the table of precedence**, not Cabinet Secretary.
 
• **Chairs NSC with voting powers** – Incorrect. The NSA **advises and coordinates security policy**; the **Prime Minister heads the National Security Council**, and voting powers are not structured this way.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role and Functions of the National Security Advisor (NSA):**

 
 
• The NSA's primary role is to act as the **chief advisor** to the Prime Minister of India on matters of national and international security.
 
• The NSA oversees the functioning of the **National Security Council (NSC)** and coordinates between multiple security agencies, including intelligence agencies like the **Research and Analysis Wing (RAW)** and the **Intelligence Bureau (IB)**.
 
• In India, the NSA plays a pivotal role in formulating and executing policies on **counter-terrorism, cyber security, and defense strategy**.
 
 
 
• **Ajit Doval's Career Highlights:**
 
 
• Ajit Doval is a former officer of the **Indian Police Service (IPS)**, 1968 batch, Kerala cadre, and has been involved in numerous high-stakes intelligence and security operations.
 
• He served as the **Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB)** and specialized in operations and counterterrorism.
 
• Doval is credited with several successful operations, including the **rescue of hostages from the Golden Temple** during Operation Black Thunder in 1988.
 
 
 
• **National Security Council (NSC):**
 
 
• Established in **1998**, the NSC is the apex body overseeing political, economic, energy, and strategic security concerns in India.
 
• The council comprises the Prime Minister, NSA, and other key ministers and officials, including the **Defense Minister, External Affairs Minister, and Home Minister**.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Secretary Rank:**
 
 
• The Cabinet Secretary is the **highest-ranking civil servant** and the chief of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS).
 
• Individuals holding ranks equivalent to the Cabinet Secretary, such as the NSA, enjoy a position of **supreme authority in their domain** and report directly to the Prime Minister.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The NSA in India is a political appointee, unlike in some other countries where it is a career position.
 
• Ajit Doval is the **fifth NSA of India** and the first to receive a **Cabinet rank**, reflecting the importance of his role in the government.
 
• The NSA plays a critical role in India's foreign policy, especially in managing **relations with neighboring countries** and handling crises.

questions.question: Under Article 258A of the Constitution, States are empowered to:

options.text: Entrust Union functions to State officers with consent
Transfer State duties to Union officers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transfer State duties to Union officers**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor of a State** can entrust functions to the **Union Government or its officers**.
 
• This can be done **only with the consent of the Government of India**.
 
• The functions may be given **conditionally or unconditionally**.
 
• These functions must relate to matters where the **executive power of the State extends**.
 
• This article is particularly utilized in situations where administrative efficiency and resource optimization are required for implementing Union functions at the state level.
 
• Unlike Article 258, which allows the President to delegate Union functions to States, Article 258A specifically focuses on entrusting functions to **State officers** with consent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 258 vs Article 258A:**

 
 
• **Article 258:** The President can entrust Union functions to the State Government or its officers without requiring the consent of the State Government.
 
• **Article 258A:** The Union Government can entrust functions to State officers only with the consent of the State Government, ensuring mutual agreement.
 
 
 
• **Federal Structure:**
 
 
• India follows a **quasi-federal structure** where powers are divided between the Union and State Governments.
 
• Articles like 258A help maintain a balance by allowing administrative collaboration while respecting the autonomy of both the Union and the States.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Entrustment:**
 
 
• Entrusting the implementation of **Union health schemes** to State health officers to ensure better execution at the grassroots level.
 
• Delegating tasks such as conducting **surveys, census, or disaster management activities** at the state level.
 
 
 
• **Union-State Relations:**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution provides for **legislative, administrative, and financial relations** between the Union and State Governments under Part XI of the Constitution.
 
• Articles like 258 and 258A promote administrative flexibility and the smooth functioning of governance in matters of national importance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Relevant Articles:**

 
 
• **Article 256:** It obligates the States to comply with the laws made by Parliament and the Union Government's executive powers.
 
• **Article 257:** This limits the States' executive power to ensure it does not interfere with the Union's executive power.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**
 
 
• The courts have upheld the importance of Articles 258 and 258A in promoting cooperative federalism.
 
• They ensure that administrative efficiency is prioritized while maintaining the sanctity of the federal structure.

questions.question: What new feature was added to the 2023 Logistics Performance Index?

options.text: Trade speed indicators using big data

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trade speed indicators using big data**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2023 Logistics Performance Index (LPI)** introduced the use of **trade speed indicators powered by big data** to improve its analysis of logistics efficiency.
 
• These indicators utilize **real-time big data** to track the speed and efficiency of trade and logistics operations in various countries.
 
• This innovation aims to provide a more precise measure of trade performance by analyzing the **time taken for goods to move** through supply chains, including ports and customs.
 
• The use of big data enables the **World Bank** to capture logistics flows and bottlenecks more accurately, helping countries identify areas of improvement in their trade processes.
 
• This updated method goes beyond traditional survey-based approaches, ensuring a more **data-driven and actionable insight** into global logistics performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Logistics Performance Index (LPI):**

 
 
• The **LPI** is an interactive benchmarking tool created by the **World Bank** to assess the logistics performance of countries globally.
 
• It evaluates performance across six key dimensions: **customs, infrastructure, international shipments, logistics competence, tracking and tracing, and timeliness**.
 
• The LPI is published every two years, with the latest report launched in **2023**.
 
• The index is used by policymakers, businesses, and investors to improve logistics infrastructure and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Big Data in Logistics:**
 
 
• **Big data analytics** involves processing vast amounts of information to derive actionable insights for industries, including logistics.
 
• In the context of the 2023 LPI, big data is used to analyze metrics such as **shipment delays, port efficiency, and customs clearance times**.
 
• By leveraging big data, countries can identify inefficiencies and optimize their supply chain processes.
 
• Examples include tracking container movements, assessing port congestion, and monitoring trade route performance.
 
 
 
• **Other Features of the 2023 LPI:**
 
 
• The 2023 report places increased emphasis on the importance of **digitalization** and its role in enhancing logistics efficiency.
 
• It also highlights the need for **sustainable logistics practices**, urging countries to adopt environmentally friendly solutions.
 
• Countries are ranked based on their ability to adapt to technological advancements and achieve seamless trade operations.
 
 
 
• **Examples of High Performers:**
 
 
• **Germany**, **Singapore**, and **Netherlands** consistently rank high due to their advanced logistics infrastructure and efficient trade practices.
 
• Countries such as **India** and **Vietnam** have shown significant improvement in their rankings due to investments in port infrastructure and digital logistics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Focus on Data-Driven Analysis:**

 
 
• The use of big data ensures that the LPI provides a more accurate and real-time assessment of logistics performance, moving away from traditional survey-based methods.
 
• Data sources include **shipping companies, customs authorities, and port operators**, making the analysis comprehensive.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Policy Making:**
 
 
• Countries can use the findings of the LPI to improve their logistics infrastructure, streamline customs processes, and enhance trade efficiency.
 
• For example, India has used insights from past reports to develop initiatives like the **PM Gati Shakti** National Master Plan.
 
 
 
• **Real-Time Applications:**
 
 
• Big data allows stakeholders to monitor logistics operations in real time, enabling quick responses to disruptions such as port congestion or customs delays.
 
• This is critical in minimizing trade bottlenecks and ensuring timely delivery of goods.

questions.question: Which organization is monitoring the Pensilungpa Glacier in Zanskar, Ladakh?

__
 
• **Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG)**, an autonomous institute under the **Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India**, is actively monitoring the **Pensilungpa Glacier** in the **Zanskar region of Ladakh**.
 
• The institute is involved in studying the glacier's **mass balance, retreat rate, and other glaciological parameters** to understand the impacts of **climate change** on Himalayan glaciers.
 
• The **Pensilungpa Glacier** has been observed to be retreating, with significant findings pointing to the influence of **increasing temperatures and decreased precipitation levels** in the region.
 
• Field observations and satellite data are utilized by WIHG to assess the **dynamic changes** in the glacier's structure and behavior.
 
• The study of glaciers like Pensilungpa is critical to understanding the **hydrology of Himalayan rivers** and the broader implications for water resources and ecological balance. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology:**

 
 
• The institute was established in **1968** and is headquartered in **Dehradun, Uttarakhand**.
 
• Its primary objective is to conduct advanced research in **Himalayan geology**, including tectonics, glaciology, geohazards, and seismology.
 
• WIHG provides scientific expertise for **disaster mitigation** in the region, focusing on **landslides, earthquakes, and glacier-related hazards**.
 
• It collaborates with national and international organizations to study the impacts of **climate change** on the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Pensilungpa Glacier:**
 
 
• Located in the **Zanskar region of Ladakh**, the glacier is an important source of water for rivers and local ecosystems.
 
• The glacier has shown a consistent retreat over the years due to **global warming** and changes in precipitation patterns.
 
• Studies on Pensilungpa Glacier contribute to understanding **regional hydrology** and assessing water availability for nearby communities.
 
 
 
• **Other Organizations:**
 
 
• **INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services):** Focuses on **oceanography** and provides information on **oceanic and climatic conditions**.
 
• **CMFRI (Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute):** Primarily deals with the **marine fisheries sector**.
 
• **Zoological Survey of India:** Established in **1916**, it focuses on **faunal research** and conservation within India.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Glacier Studies:**
 
 
• Glaciers are critical indicators of **climate change**, as their retreat provides direct evidence of rising temperatures.
 
• Himalayan glaciers serve as water sources for major rivers like the **Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus**, impacting millions of lives.
 
• The retreat of glaciers has implications for **water security, agriculture, and disaster management** in the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Himalayas** are home to approximately **15,000 glaciers**, making them a vital area for glaciological studies.
 
• Glacier monitoring helps in predicting **flash floods, avalanches, and other glacial hazards**.
 
• India has several institutes involved in glaciological research, including the **National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)** and WIHG.
 
• Policies and initiatives like the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** aim to address the challenges posed by retreating glaciers.

questions.question: The Kármán line marks the boundary of Earth’s atmosphere at approximately:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Kármán line** is widely recognized as the boundary between Earth's atmosphere and outer space.
 
• It is located at an altitude of approximately **100 kilometers (62 miles)** above sea level.
 
• This altitude was determined by Hungarian-American engineer and physicist **Theodore von Kármán**, who calculated that at this point, the atmosphere becomes too thin to support conventional aircraft flight.
 
• The **Kármán line** is used as a reference by organizations like the **Fédération Aéronautique Internationale (FAI)** for defining outer space.
 
• It is crucial for space law and the demarcation of aerospace and outer space activities. Many space agencies, including NASA, acknowledge it as a significant boundary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theodore von Kármán:**

 
 
• Theodore von Kármán (1881–1963) was a prominent Hungarian-American physicist and engineer.
 
• He is known for his contributions to aerodynamics, specifically in the area of supersonic and hypersonic airflow.
 
• His calculations regarding the limits of atmospheric flight led to the establishment of the **Kármán line** at 100 km.
 
 
 
• **Space Boundary Recognition:**
 
 
• While the **Kármán line** is internationally recognized, the **United States** often defines space starting at **80 kilometers (50 miles)** above sea level.
 
• Despite this variation, 100 km remains the globally accepted standard for the boundary of outer space.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Layers:**
 
 
• The Earth's atmosphere is divided into several layers, including the **troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere,** and **exosphere**.
 
• The **Kármán line** lies within the transition between the **thermosphere** and the **exosphere**.
 
 
 
• **Space Law Implications:**
 
 
• The demarcation of space is essential for legal and regulatory purposes, such as **sovereignty, satellite placement, and space exploration**.
 
• The **Outer Space Treaty (1967)** does not define the exact boundary of space but implicitly acknowledges the importance of such a demarcation.
 
 
 
• **Scientific and Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding the **Kármán line** is vital for space missions, satellite launches, and aerospace technology development.
 
• It also plays a role in distinguishing between **airspace sovereignty** and international space, which is free for exploration by all nations.
